region.text: Ryazan land as Cliopatria draws it from 1094

ledger.note: 1094: the Murom-Ryazan land of Chernigov's Sviatoslavichi enters the map as Ryazan (Cliopatria's start). Murom page: 'In 1054, Yaroslav the Wise bequeathed the Principality of Chernigov to his second eldest surviving son,' and Murom and Ryazan went with it; Oleg page: 'in 1094, he returned from Tmutarakan with an armed force of Kipchaks' and took Chernigov. The pages give no founding of Ryazan in 1094: the Ryazan page says the principality 'fully split off from Chernigov' in 1129.

1129: Murom-Ryazan fully splits off from Chernigov and Yaroslav's line keeps it. The Ryazan page: 'The principality, then Murom-Ryazan, fully split off from Chernigov' in 1129 and 'Yaroslav's line kept it after he died that year'; the Murom page has Yaroslav Sviatoslavich ruling there from 1127 ('it became a separate principality') and his sons Sviatoslav and Rostislav receiving Murom and Ryazan in 1129. Ryazan later separated from Murom (the Murom page gives no year); until 1212 the princes were not grand princes.

ledger.note: 1237: the Mongols take Ryazan, the first Rus' principality hit. 'And the Tartars took the town [of Ryazan] on December 21'; the Ryazan page: 'In December 1237, the duchy became the first of all other former states of' Rus' to suffer the invasion, 'much of the princely family was killed, and the capital was destroyed.'

region.text: Ryazan land, overrun by Batu in December 1237 and early 1238

ledger.note: 1238: the Mongol campaign in the Ryazan land ends. The capital fell on 21 December 1237 ('the Tartars took the town on December 21', Mongol invasion page), and in 1238 the remaining Ryazan forces joined the Vladimir-Suzdal army against Batu near Kolomna (Ryazan page); the horde laid siege to Vladimir on 4 February 1238 'having burnt down Kolomna and Moscow'. The year matches this dossier's war (1237-1238) and the mongol-empire dossier's contest_end of December 1237. The principality survived as a Horde vassal (Ryazan page: rulers 1237-1301, 1371, 1380, 1520). [Reviewer eu-16-c: year moved from 1240, Cliopatria's row end, to the page's 1238.]

The page keeps it as one state: after the Mongol conquest of December 1237 ('The duchy was completely overrun, with almost the whole princely family killed, the capital destroyed') its princes ruled 'as their vassal' (Oleg the Red, 1252-1258) and 'as Mongol vassal' (Roman III, 1258-1270); Daniel of Moscow 'took Ryazan' in 1301; Murom 'was taken by Moscow in 1392'; Ivan III (1427-1456) 'renounced his allegiance to Golden Horde'; and 'in 1521, the Ryazan Principality was merged with Muscovy'. The year 1452 is the schema's join with 'ryazan' (found 1453), not a page date. The page dates no 'Grand Principality' title and no capital move, so no rename or capital_move is added.

wars.name: Oleg's Murom campaign against Monomakh
wars.outcome: Oleg killed Monomakh's son Iziaslav at Murom in 1096 and was pushed back to Murom by Mstislav Monomakhovich; the war ended with the compromise of the Council of Liubech (19 October 1097), which left Chernigov, Tmutarakan, Ryazan and Murom to the Sviatoslavichi.
wars.note: Murom lies outside Cliopatria's Ryazan shape and has no Cliopatria row, so no contest zone is drawn. The Murom page says Murom changed hands seven times between 1077 and 1097.

wars.name: Vladimir-Suzdal's wars on Ryazan
wars.outcome: Ryazan's forces were defeated in 1177; Vsevolod III 'punished the princes of Ryazan by ousting them from their lands' in 1180 and 1187 and burned Ryazan and Belgorod in 1207; Roman I ruled Ryazan as Vsevolod's vassal (1180-1207) and died in captivity; Ryazan became independent after Vsevolod's death in 1212.
wars.note: Ryazan page: the city 'was burned twice in a span of twenty years from 1186 to 1208'; Vsevolod page: 1180, 1187, 1207; Vladimir-Suzdal page: defeat in 1177 and resistance 'put down in 1180, 1187, and 1202'; Murom page: independence in 1212. The vassalage is recorded in the principality-of-rostov-suzdal dossier (vassal_start 1180, vassal_end 1212).

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Ryazan
wars.outcome: Ryazan fell on 21 December 1237 and its capital was destroyed; some Ryazan forces joined the Vladimir-Suzdal army against Batu near Kolomna in 1238.
wars.note: The Battle of the Voronezh is not on the pages opened.

Cliopatria shape fault: the Ryazan shape contains Vladimir and the Klyazma valley (and the Rostov-Suzdal shape has a hole there); the correction removes a 70 km disc round Vladimir and the same disc is added to Rostov-Suzdal (Vladimir is also outside Cliopatria's Vladimir-Suzdal shapes of 1294 and 1363, so the hole runs through the later rows). Not settled: whether the Voronezh-Lipetsk south (steppe) and the Meshchera north of the Oka belonged to Ryazan; Murom (separate principality, no Cliopatria row, 'principality-of-murom' suggested) is outside the shape; Kolomna was Ryazan's before 1301 (Moscow page) but is outside the shape. The vassalage of Ryazan to Vladimir-Suzdal (1180-1212) is in the rostov-suzdal dossier. Start 1094 is Cliopatria's; the pages say 1127 (Murom) and 1129 (Ryazan). The Battle of the Voronezh and the 1217-1218 Cuman-backed massacres are not drawn. Gazetteer names needed: Old Ryazan (place, about 54.37N 40.10E, Spassky district), Murom is present in the gazetteer. FX-51 (2 Nov 2026, life-span gap): the dossier no longer ends in 1240. The page keeps one state from 1129 to the merger of 1521 and the later row 'ryazan' (found 1453, counterpart this slug) starts the Cliopatria shape again, so the dissolve moved from 1240 (into mongol-empire) to 1452 (into ryazan) and a keyframe principality-of-ryazan_1241 holds the 1236 shape minus Vladimir for 1241-1452 (confidence 1 for its extent). Mongol overlordship (Mongol Empire, then Golden Horde) is for data/hierarchy.csv. The jump from 65,560 km2 (here) to 17,026 km2 (Cliopatria 'Ryazan' 1453) is not dated by any page.
